_comment: Deny rules merged into ~/.claude/settings.json by install.ps1.
Deny takes precedence over allow and over every permission mode,
including auto and bypass. These rules do not depend on Python, so they
keep working even if the guard hook fails to start. They are the floor.
Two kinds of rule are NOT here, because both are generated at install
time from the machine's own configuration: a pair per protected folder
name, and one per entry in BLOCKED_PROGRAMS in data_guard.py. The full
list that was actually installed is written to guard_config.json as
installed_deny_rules, which is what uninstall.ps1 removes.
'retired' holds rules earlier versions installed. install.ps1 subtracts
them and uninstall.ps1 removes them, so a machine that already has them
is cleaned up rather than left carrying a rule nothing maintains.
